questions: Did these eye-movement abnormalities begin suddenly, within hours or a day?
Do you currently have difficulty walking or keeping your balance?
Do you have new slurred speech or difficulty coordinating your arms or legs?
Do you have double vision or trouble controlling your eye movements?
Do you have new weakness, numbness, facial drooping, or difficulty swallowing?
Did you develop a sudden severe headache, vomiting, or loss of consciousness?
Have you recently started, stopped, or changed the dose of any medication?
Have you recently taken sedatives, sleeping pills, anti-seizure medication, lithium, or recreational drugs?
Have you had unusually heavy alcohol use or abrupt alcohol withdrawal recently?
Have you had spinning dizziness, hearing loss, or ringing in either ear?
Have you had episodes like this before?
Have you ever been diagnosed with multiple sclerosis, a cerebellar disorder, or another neurological disease?
Do you have a history of migraine?
Have you recently had a head injury or infection?
Do close family members have unexplained balance problems, abnormal eye movements, or a progressive neurological disorder?
Have you had unexplained weight loss, cancer, or treatment that weakens your immune system?

dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Anti-Homer3 antibody–associated autoimmune cerebellar ataxia (immune-mediated, non-paraneoplastic cause not yet established)

ALTERNATIVE: Paraneoplastic cerebellar degeneration with anti-Homer3 antibodies

ALTERNATIVE: Seronegative or antibody-negative autoimmune cerebellar ataxia with a coincidental anti-Homer3 result

ALTERNATIVE: Episodic ataxia type 2 or another hereditary cerebellar ataxia not detected by the performed genetic testing
